business_problem: World Rugby wanted to make the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 more engaging by unlocking and activating complex match data in real time so broadcasters, commentators, and digital channels could give fans richer insights and better storytelling during matches.
solution_summary: World Rugby, Capgemini, Stats Perform, and AWS built TryZone IQ as a generative AI platform for live rugby insight generation. The implementation ingests historical and live Opta match data delivered in real time by Stats Perform, then routes that data into generative AI models hosted on Amazon Bedrock to produce short, match-ready narratives about player impact, team trends, and standout performances. TryZone IQ acts as the orchestration and delivery layer, packaging those model outputs for editorial use. Before distribution, analysts review and approve the generated insights to maintain quality and relevance. Approved insights are then pushed into the live broadcast production workflow for commentators and on-screen graphics, and also published to World Rugby’s online and in-app Match Center plus social channels. The source does not name a separate storage service, so storage is not attributed beyond the historical and live data inputs.

data_flow: Historical and live Opta match data is delivered in real time by Stats Perform into TryZone IQ, where generative AI models hosted on Amazon Bedrock create summaries of player impact, team trends, and standout performances. Analysts review and approve the outputs, which are then fed into live broadcast production, World Rugby’s Match Center, in-app digital experiences, and social media clips.
integration_points: World Rugby online and in-app digital platforms
business_outcome: The platform helped World Rugby deliver a more engaging broadcast and digital fan experience with real-time AI-generated commentary insights during the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, and it was later extended to other rugby competitions and additional languages.
